blocks.text:
The architectural refinement of Buenos Aires rivals only Paris, yet the city's beauty is entirely its own. The tour introduces you to the old quarter of La Boca, the historic San Telmo district with its antiques market on Plaza Dorrego, the central Plaza de Mayo and the Casa Rosada presidential palace, the city's 67-meter obelisk on Avenida 9 de Julio, the elegant Recoleta neighborhood with its famous cemetery and Our Lady of Pilar church, and the modern Puerto Madero district and city parks.

In the evening — a tango show with dinner. Tango is beloved the world over, but Argentina holds one undeniable advantage — this is where it was born. The dance originated in the city's port districts, among poor immigrants, gaucho herdsmen and other displaced people; originally danced by two men in a fairly unrestrained style, its name comes from the Latin "tangere" — to touch. Over time, tango grew slower and gained new tones of intimacy, orchestras devoted to tango emerged, and today it remains one of the most sensual dances on Earth. At the restaurant, the interior evokes the spirit of tango, and a menu of traditional dishes paired with fine Argentine wines completes this romantic evening.
